# Receipt fixtures

The single copies are built by `examples/receipt/build_fixtures.sh CAPSULE_CLI_CHECKOUT` through the real
capsulectl, at capsule-cli `fde7ee0d29df980f7b202376023bc575f8794a37`. Synthetic: capsule-cli's
retail-checkout demo (an example shop, an example item), generated keys, no account or
session identifiers.

| Files | What they are |
| --- | --- |
| `keep.*`, `counterparty.*`, `adjudicator.*` | One deal and the three copies capsulectl cuts of it: the user's own (`keep`) and the shared copies for the other party and for an adjudicator. The same records, at the same log places, in all three; the share builder withheld what each audience must not get. |
| `golden-2.bundle.json`, `golden-2.snapshot.json` | capsule-cli's presentation golden for the unilateral receipt (`internal/cli/testdata/presentation/2-unilateral-receipt`), unchanged: the bundle, and the text deal-view.js showed for it, in order. `tests/test_receipt_golden.py` accounts for every line. |
| `bilateral-*.bundle.json` | Built by `examples/receipt/build_bilateral_fixtures.sh CAPSULE_CLI_CHECKOUT 53b9bdce7ab773f36271be1d3385cfb3dc94ae0b`. One synthetic deal seen by both parties: the buyer's agent (the retail-checkout demo) and the shop's agent recording the same sale (offer, the buyer's acceptance, commit; typed records). `compose_bilateral.py` puts two copies, byte for byte, into a `composed/v1` container capsulectl sealed and checkpointed: `-counterparty` (both counterparty copies, one agreeing join), `-adjudicator` (both adjudicator copies, an agreeing and a mismatching join), `-keep` (the buyer's own copy beside the seller's counterparty copy) and `-two-deals` (the buyer's counterparty copy beside a seller copy of another deal). No producer agrees one deal id between two parties yet, so the capsulectl built for these takes the deal id from `CAPSULE_FIXTURE_DEAL_ID` (a one-line change to a copy of the checkout, applied by the script). The joins are on the copies' root records and are the fixture composer's choice; the observers' roles and custody domains are declared by it. |
| `one-sided-*.bundle.json` | `one-sided-keep` and `one-sided-counterparty`: `examples/receipt/one_sided.py bilateral-<audience>.bundle.json absence`. `one-sided-refusal-keep`: the same over `bilateral-keep` with `refusal`, a refusal signed in capsulectl's `ed25519-jcs` form with a fixed synthetic key, which capsulectl verifies and reads INCOMPLETE. For the absence ones: each is the bilateral fixture with the seller's member replaced by an `absence` (the holder asked for the seller's copy and nothing came back between 2026-10-09T18:00Z and 2026-10-12T18:00Z; synthetic), every join declared `one_sided` and the composed digest recomputed. The container and the buyer's copy are unchanged. Verified by capsulectl built from capsule-cli main `5745be57`, which derives the join `one_sided` and passes the composition. |
| `seller-*.bundle.json` (not `-producer-`) | Built by `examples/receipt/build_seller_fixtures.sh CAPSULE_CLI_CHECKOUT 53b702f7d673207f1f016dae27cca285a35d51ac`. One synthetic sale of an example bicycle (ask 1900, a floor of 1700) with two buyer threads, sealed by the seller's agent in typed records. `seller-keep`, `-counterparty`, `-adjudicator`: thread A's three copies (a statement of the item's condition, an offer at 2000 superseded by one at 1900, the buyer's acceptance of the 1900 offer, the commit, a pickup address given once the user approved, the card processor's evidence, the close with what was handed over). `seller-declined`: thread B's counterparty copy (an offer under the floor, never answered, then closed not_selected). `seller-bilateral`: the counterparty copy of a buyer's own deal for the same bicycle beside thread A's counterparty copy, composed as the bilateral fixtures are, one agreeing join (the same deal id by the same `CAPSULE_FIXTURE_DEAL_ID` change). FIXTURE STEP: capsulectl at that commit does not engage the seller kind `x-deal-seller/v0`, so `engage_seller_kind.py` adds it to each seller copy after capsulectl cut it; it refuses once capsulectl engages any extension kind it did not engage then, and for a copy whose opening record does not seal `party_role` `seller`. |
| `seller-producer-*.bundle.json`, `buyer-producer-counterparty.bundle.json` | capsulectl's own copies, from the capsule-cli branch that engages `x-deal-seller/v0` (its pull request not yet merged): one typed seller deal (offer, the buyer's exact acceptance, commit) cut for each audience, the kind engaged by the producer; and a buyer's deal's counterparty copy, which engages nothing new. Copied unchanged except for key order (`jq -S`). Synthetic parties and demo keys. |
| The bilateral fixtures' seller copies | `examples/receipt/recompose_engaged.py` applied the same fixture step to the seller copy inside each `bilateral-*` bundle after `build_bilateral_fixtures.sh` built it, and recomputed that member's digest and the composed digest; nothing else changed. `build_bilateral_fixtures.sh` now applies the step itself, so a rebuild yields the same shape. |
| `main-standalone-*.bundle.json` | Cut by `examples/receipt/cut_standalone_bundles.sh CAPSULECTL CAPSULECTL_DEAL` with capsulectl built from capsule-cli main `d8f58012` and the deal plugin from evidencebook-deal main `37071b3`. One errand (an example desk lamp: the ask with no merchant, a search, a dead end, a shortlist, a recommendation, a pick, a switch to another shop, a pause, the user's OK, the payment). The copies carry the report as capsulectl seals it today, a standalone record in `x-deal-report/v0` on no log (capsule-cli#294): `-keep` is the owner's copy, `-counterparty` the one shared with the other party. Synthetic parties, generated keys. `capsulectl-journey-words.json` copies capsule-cli's `journey.*` wording (the receipt pack's set is held equal to it); `main-standalone-keep.deal-view-journey.json` is the rows capsulectl's own deal page (deal-view.js) shows under "How it went" for `main-standalone-keep`, read in a browser from the page `cut_standalone_bundles.sh ... KEEP_DIR` wrote. |
| `main-*.bundle.json` | Cut by `examples/receipt/cut_main_bundles.sh CAPSULE_CLI_CHECKOUT CAPSULECTL` with capsulectl built from capsule-cli main `e9b1f21d` (unpatched; no fixture step: capsulectl engages `x-deal-seller/v0` on a seller's copies itself). `main-buyer-keep` / `-counterparty`: the retail-checkout demo deal, the owner's copy (`deal report --bundle`) and the copy shared with the other party (`deal report --share counterparty`, whose bundle is the one its page carries). `main-seller-keep` / `-counterparty`: a sale of an example bicycle (`deal sale new`, one thread opened with `deal open --sale`: a statement of condition, an approved offer, the buyer's acceptance, the commit, the close), cut the same way. Synthetic parties, generated keys. |
| `mesh-payer-selected.*` | A Mesh node's payer-side deal, cut from one shared ledger by the capsules-plugin `deal-receipt-bundle` route (Mesh-LLM/capsules-plugin#145; report sealed `keep` by #150, `27074e3`): the deal's baseline, outcome, close and keep-audience report, producer-selected (no range proof), a test node's generated keys and a synthetic exchange. `mesh-payer-selected.verify.json` is what `capsulectl verify --bundle` reported (capsule-cli `4e96d2c`): verdict INCOMPLETE, every claim `pass` but `interval_coverage` `withheld` with `selection_not_checkable`. |
| `mesh-provider-selected.*` | A Mesh node's own half of a paid exchange it served, cut by capsules-plugin's `provider-receipt-bundle` route (Mesh-LLM/capsules-plugin#134): the exchange record it served and its two `payee_observed` legs (995 msat received, 5 msat fee each), producer-selected, no payload disclosed; a test node's generated keys. Not a deal, so none of the deal receipt modules renders it; `capsule_viewer.receipt.provider` does. `.verify.json` is what `capsulectl verify --bundle` reported (capsule-cli `4e96d2c`): INCOMPLETE, `selection_not_checkable` only. |
| `disjointness.json` | The receipt registry's resolve output for four of the fixtures above, one per role x composition (`keep`, `bilateral-keep`, `seller-keep`, `seller-bilateral`): per receipt module whether it matches and every manifest clause it fails, and the resolution. Written by `python tests/test_receipt_disjointness.py`; that test checks it is current. |
| `<name>.verify.json` | What `capsulectl verify --bundle` reported for that bundle, as written. The seller, producer and recomposed bilateral fixtures were verified by capsulectl built from capsule-cli `53b702f7d673207f1f016dae27cca285a35d51ac`, which reports the seller kind as `uninterpreted`. The module's context is built from it; nothing in this package verifies. |

`../aac-presentation/` vendors agent-action-capsule's manifest schema
(`schemas/presentation-manifest-v0.json`), its built-in manifests and three example
manifests from `schemas/examples/presentation-manifest-v0/`, at agent-action-capsule
`67b056c`.
